en: A quay at low tide, a man with an errand, and a weir that somebody wants opened.
Norrel wants the gate at the weir opened. He wants to be paid back in person, and he wants to be alive to do the paying.
The tide is out and the quay smells of it. Boards, rope, a lockbox nobody has bothered to move, and one man standing where he can watch the road.
Somebody has been at the mud by the sea wall. The quay is quieter than it was, and stays quieter.
He prices you the way he would price a boat: quickly, and without looking at your face while he does it.
Salt has been at the hasp for years. It would open for anybody who cared to try, which is its own kind of answer.
Fresh earth, and not much of it. Whoever dug this was in a hurry and did not expect to be asked about it.
Two of them are up on the hurdles where the water runs fastest, and they have seen you before you have finished seeing them.
Nothing is standing. The weir makes the noise a weir makes, which is the first honest sound all day.
The gate is seized with rust and weed. It would go, with a key, or with somebody sufficiently annoyed.
The gate lifts a hand's width and the marsh lets go of the whole of it at once, downstream, loudly.
The causeway goes under at the ford, and they were waiting on the far side of it, which means somebody told them you were coming.
A boat is pulled up the bank with nothing in it and nobody near it. It has been there long enough for the grass to grow round the keel.
Halfway along, the causeway narrows to a ford, and the water on both sides of it has stopped making the noise water makes.
